Dinner with a difference
May 2019 • Solo
This small caravan with street seating serves up ramen, noodles and bhan mí. The food is tasty and reasonably priced; if your nervous about eating street food but want to experience a street food vibe, this is the place to come. 

I ate the pork bhan mí - the baguette was crispy on the outside with soft, fluffy bread inside - the perfect combination of crunchy and soft. The stewed pork filling was tender with a superb balance of sweet and spicy. I washed this down with a Saigon beer.

This place had seen better days
Dec 2018 • Solo
Till I visited this restaurant, I thought ALL Japanese are ultra-clean. The disgusting table mats had never tasted soap since the they were bought. Either it was good and clean earlier and stopped being so now or the other reviews were too drunk on cheap Vietnamese beer to notice. Awful and unhygienic - not the words I associate with anything to do with Japan.

Banh My was terrible - half of the pork in it ended up between my teeth, extremely stringy and chewy and perhaps stale too. I had to floss twice to get rid of half of it. 

I'd never forgive these clowns for messing with my time and the slice of my life I gave them - especially considering the fact that I walked 4 miles return to eat there reading the reviews. I could have easily eaten in any restaurant in the old quarters and assuredly have had a better lunch.

Passable ramen
Oct 2017 • Couples
Visit only if you are desperate for ramen! 
The ramen was okay, the flavor of the broth was on the bland side, the noodles were decent, and the toppings were flavorless. It is understandable that this is a ramen place in Hanoi, but for the price (70k) and the dish that came out, we were disappointed. The restaurant itself is nice, there is a outside bar type of dining area on first floor and a few tables and window seats on the second floor. Just a heads up, there is a sign outside that says free AC upstairs, but upon entering and eating, no AC was turned on. So we ended up eating sub par noodles while sweating on the second floor.
If you want good ramen, visit Japan!
